title: health-signal-windowing-and-autoscaler-hysteresis-for-stable-slos
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We have seen flapping autoscaler behavior and noisy failovers in multi-region tests where brief latency spikes or transient KV cache misses trigger pod readiness toggles and cascading scale-ups/downs. This increases cost and causes transient SLO breaches (P99 and error-rate targets) during traffic spikes. Goal: Introduce a composite health signal and autoscaler hysteresis to make readiness/liveness checks and scale decisions more robust while preserving fast failover for true outages. This ticket implements health-signal windowing, EWMA smoothing, readiness 'soft-fail' semantics, autoscaler stabilization settings, circuit-breaker thresholds, and a controlled load-shedding policy to keep SLOs intact under overload.
acceptance_criteria: Composite health signal implemented and exposed as "service.health_score" metric (0-100) with 30s granularity
Kubernetes readiness probe replaced by a controlled soft-fail that drains traffic over a 20s grace window instead of immediate 503s
Autoscaler uses stabilizationWindowSeconds=45 and targetUtilization smoothing; production canary shows reduced scale flapping in 3 synthetic spike tests
Circuit breaker triggers when rolling 1m error-rate > 5% OR P99 latency > 5s; trigger recorded in tracing and Dashboard alert fires
Load-shedding returns 429 with Retry-After for best-effort requests and 503 for critical path failures; overall user-visible error rate stays below SLO thresholds during overload runs
SLO dashboards reflect <1.5x variance in cost-per-token under spike testing compared to current baseline and maintain P99 latency objective
tasks: Design composite health signal (latency windows, error-rate, kv-cache-hit, instance-ready-age) - doc in Confluence
Implement EWMA smoothing and 30s rolling-window aggregator in runtime health agent
Change readiness probe to call internal /health/ready which implements soft-fail drain and exposes last_good_timestamp
Add autoscaler stabilization settings and hysteresis hooks in control plane
Implement circuit breaker with metrics-based open/close and integration with global LB for failover decisions
Add configurable load-shedding policy: priority classes, token-bucket admission, 429/Retry-After responses
Create canary plan and run 3 synthetic spike scenarios (ramp, burst, region-failover) and capture dashboards
Update SLO doc and runbook; add postmortem template for any regressions
Create PRs, test in staging, and collect perf/latency traces for review
decisions: Use 2-minute sliding window for primary health signal but compute sub-signals at 30s resolution to capture short spikes
Apply EWMA smoothing with alpha=0.25 for latency-based sub-signal to reduce reaction to single bad samples
Readiness soft-fail semantics: drain for 20s by returning 200 with X-Drain header until complete; only change endpoint to fail (503) after 20s if not recovered
Autoscaler stabilization window set to 45s to reduce oscillation; scale-up still allowed aggressively if health_score < 30
Circuit breaker opens on 1-minute rolling error-rate >5% OR sustained P99 >5s; automatic half-open after 60s with 10% probe traffic
Load-shedding returns 429 for non-critical traffic with Retry-After; critical API paths are protected and only shed last (best-effort) priority
Multi-region failover: prefer active-active routing with weight shifting; only failover entire region if health_score < 10 for >120s
